headlines.title: TURMOIL AT WORLDCOM: THE OVERVIEW; WORLDCOM FACING CHARGES OF FRAUD; INQUIRIES EXPAND
headlines.abstract: SEC files fraud charges against WorldCom, and Pres Bush vows to hold people accountable for bookkeeping scandal at company; SEC says accounting scheme intended to manipulate earnings to meet Wall Street's expectations and support stock price may have been blessed by executives other than Scott D Sullivan, chief financial officer, and David Myers, controller, both of whom have been dismissed; Nasdaq exchange suspends trading of WorldCom shares and tracking stock of its MCI unit; value of WorldCom bonds plunge, and likelihood of bankruptcy filing increases; Justice Department and House committee open investigations; company's work force braces for wave of layoffs; some consumer and corporate customers of WorldCom's MCI long-distance unit are already looking for alternative carriers, but telecommunications stocks are battered nevertheless; photos (M)

headlines.title: TURMOIL AT WORLDCOM: THE FINANCE EXECUTIVE; From Low Profile to No Profile
headlines.abstract: WorldCom Inc's former chief financial officer Scott D Sullivan, who was 'whiz kid' Bernard J Ebbers relied on to put together many mergers that lifted WorldCom from obscurity as small long-distance phone company to prominence as global telecommunications giant, has dropped from public view, leaving deepening mystery about his actions; Securities and Exchange Commission says it plans to file fraud charges against Sullivan and other WorldCom executives; Jeffries & Co analyst Richard Klugman says Sullivan 'was the most credible CFO in the entire industry'; chief executive John W Sidgmore, who took over as chief executive when Ebbers resigned, says company had been 'shocked' when accounting transgressions it reported this week were uncovered during review of previous financial statements; records show most stock sales by WorldCom insiders occurred before 2000; chart; photos (M)
